comments.text:
I have a hard time aligning with your issues. I started my career young. I started working at 16. I had 4 part time jobs in High-school before graduation. One was in HVAC and one was in Telecommunications. 

You have to teach your kids to learn a high paying talent, skill, or get an accredited college degree. I met with my guidance counselor throughout my High-school years. I had meetings with my OJT (On Job Training) instructor for High-school. Proper guidance and knowledge is extremely important!

 I did all I could when I was still under 18. I had worked almost 35 hours combined  per week while finishing High-school. Before graduation I had two career paths. Siemens Telecommunications AS Degree/Apprentice or HVAC Technician with my own van for one of Orlando's largest HVAC company. 

I chose the Telecommunications path because the job was mostly indoors and they promised they would pay for my Bachelors Degree and Beyond. 

13 years later I had my bachelor's degree making over $60,000. I also had a  part time business on the side making $30,000 working an average 40 hours per month. 

I quit that company and went to work for another company for 7 years and still operating my business on my mornings off or weekends. During that time I spent 21months getting my Masters in Business Degree that company paid for it all. 

The key is to work on tapping into as many resources available to you and working towards that direction. All my degrees were free. I never had a school loan. I don't owe anyone! 

I retired at 41. I own properties and live a more laid back life because I hustled and got my education out the way earlier in life. This is America. I am a Naturalized Citizen who came here at infant age and achieved the American dream. I want to see you  do it too.

Hi, shall I share my experience? I will, even though nobody will read it among all these funny comments.

So, I live in Italy. Life here is not as expensive as in the US, not even as expensive as in other European countries, but still, euros and dollars are valued about the same. Prices here in Italy are about 40% lower than in the US. Just for reference, rent here starts from 700€ a month; at least 100€ a month for bills; car fuel and insurance aren't cheap here, I pay 250€ a month at least. Then there's food, taxes, and so on. Now, this might not be the average experience, but it's very common for a beginner to get paid between 500€ and 800€ a month in Italy (before taxes!).

Me? I started with about 2€/hour, or 320€/month as an animator -.-

After 5 years of struggles, I had a lot of success... Now I am an animator supervisor, so I get to be paid 1500€/month -.-

We are all basically slaves 😮‍💨
